source: Short notes on well-known dates, written for this app.
events: ARPANET switches to TCP/IP, the protocols the internet still runs on.
Luna 1 is launched, the first spacecraft to reach the Moon's neighbourhood.
Apple Computer is incorporated.
Sputnik 1 falls back to Earth and burns up after three months in orbit.
Henry Ford announces the five-dollar, eight-hour working day.
New Mexico becomes the 47th state of the United States.
Galileo observes the four largest moons of Jupiter.
Elvis Presley is born in Tupelo, Mississippi.
Steve Jobs unveils the first iPhone.
The London Underground, the world's first underground railway, opens.
Insulin is used to treat diabetes in a person for the first time, in Toronto.
A long-distance radio message is sent from the Eiffel Tower for the first time.
Johnny Cash records his live album at Folsom Prison.
The Huygens probe lands on Titan, Saturn's largest moon.
Wikipedia goes online.
Prohibition begins in the United States.
Benjamin Franklin is born in Boston.
Eugene Ely lands an aeroplane on a ship's deck for the first time.
Georges Claude patents the neon lighting tube.
John F. Kennedy is inaugurated: "Ask not what your country can do for you."
USS Nautilus, the first nuclear submarine, is launched.
Apple's "1984" commercial airs during the Super Bowl.
The bathyscaphe Trieste reaches the bottom of the Mariana Trench.
Gold is found at Sutter's Mill, starting the California Gold Rush.
The first Winter Olympic Games open in Chamonix.
The First Fleet lands at Sydney Cove.
The Outer Space Treaty is signed in Washington, London and Moscow.
The Space Shuttle Challenger breaks apart 73 seconds after launch.
Karl Benz patents the first petrol-powered automobile.
The Beatles play their last concert, on the roof of Apple Corps in London.
Explorer 1, the first American satellite, is launched.
The first volume of the Oxford English Dictionary is published.
The first Groundhog Day is observed in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania.
Luna 9 makes the first soft landing on the Moon.
Facebook is launched from a Harvard dorm room.
Apollo 14 lands on the Moon.
Elizabeth II becomes queen on the death of George VI.
The Beatles arrive in the United States for the first time.
Jules Verne is born in Nantes.
William G. Morgan invents volleyball in Holyoke, Massachusetts.
Deep Blue beats Garry Kasparov in a game of chess for the first time.
Nelson Mandela is released after 27 years in prison.
Charles Darwin and Abraham Lincoln are born on the same day.
Galileo arrives in Rome for his trial before the Inquisition.
Alexander Graham Bell applies for a patent on the telephone.
Galileo Galilei is born in Pisa.
Howard Carter opens the burial chamber of Tutankhamun.
Vanguard 2, the first weather satellite, is launched.
Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto.
Nicolaus Copernicus is born in Torun.
John Glenn becomes the first American to orbit the Earth.
Edwin Land demonstrates the Polaroid instant camera.
George Washington is born in Virginia.
The Gutenberg Bible is published, by tradition.
Pope Gregory XIII announces the Gregorian calendar.
Samuel Colt patents the revolver.
Robert Watson-Watt demonstrates that radio waves can detect an aircraft.
James Chadwick announces the discovery of the neutron.
Watson and Crick announce they have worked out the structure of DNA.
Hattie McDaniel becomes the first African American to win an Oscar.
Yellowstone becomes the world's first national park.
Concorde makes its first flight, from Toulouse.
Alexander Graham Bell is born in Edinburgh.
The United States Constitution comes into effect.
Churchill gives his "Iron Curtain" speech in Fulton, Missouri.
Michelangelo is born in Caprese.
Alexander Graham Bell is granted the patent for the telephone.
The New York Stock Exchange is founded.
The Barbie doll makes its debut at the American International Toy Fair.
Bell makes the first telephone call: "Mr Watson, come here, I want to see you."
Mikhail Gorbachev becomes leader of the Soviet Union.
Tim Berners-Lee submits his proposal for what becomes the World Wide Web.
William Herschel discovers Uranus.
Albert Einstein is born in Ulm. It is also Pi Day.
44 BC
Julius Caesar is assassinated on the Ides of March.
Robert Goddard launches the first liquid-fuelled rocket.
Saint Patrick dies, by tradition; the day became his feast.
Alexei Leonov makes the first spacewalk.
Nevada legalises gambling.
Einstein's general theory of relativity is published.
The first tweet is posted: "just setting up my twttr".
The Lumiere brothers show a motion picture to an audience for the first time.
The Mir space station re-enters and breaks up over the Pacific.
Robert Koch announces the discovery of the bacterium that causes tuberculosis.
Christiaan Huygens discovers Titan.
Jonas Salk announces his polio vaccine.
Marconi sends the first radio message across the English Channel.
Constantinople and Angora are renamed Istanbul and Ankara.
Mariner 10 becomes the first spacecraft to fly past Mercury.
Hymen Lipman patents the pencil with an eraser on the end.
The Eiffel Tower is inaugurated.
Apple Computer is founded by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne.
Beethoven's First Symphony is premiered in Vienna.
Martin Cooper makes the first call from a handheld mobile phone.
Microsoft is founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen.
Jacob Roggeveen sights Easter Island, on Easter Sunday.
The first modern Olympic Games open in Athens.
The World Health Organization is founded.
The Venus de Milo is discovered on the island of Milos.
The earliest known recording of a human voice is made, in Paris.
The Titanic sets sail from Southampton.
Apollo 13 is launched.
Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space.
An oxygen tank explodes aboard Apollo 13: "Houston, we've had a problem."
The Human Genome Project is declared complete.
Leonardo da Vinci is born in Vinci.
Wilbur Wright is born in Indiana.
Apollo 13 returns safely to Earth.
The first crossword puzzle book is published by Simon and Schuster.
Salyut 1, the first space station, is launched.
Marie and Pierre Curie isolate radium chloride.
753 BC
Rome is founded, by tradition.
The first Earth Day is held.
William Shakespeare dies; the 23rd is also his traditional birthday.
The Hubble Space Telescope is launched.
Watson and Crick's paper on the structure of DNA is published in Nature.
Field trials of the Salk polio vaccine begin.
The universe is created, according to a calculation by Johannes Kepler.
Thor Heyerdahl sets sail across the Pacific on the raft Kon-Tiki.
The first edition of Roget's Thesaurus is published.
CERN puts the World Wide Web software into the public domain.
The Empire State Building opens.
The first commercial jet airliner service begins, with the de Havilland Comet.
The first spam email is sent, to ARPANET users.
Margaret Thatcher becomes prime minister. May the Fourth is also Star Wars Day.
Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space.
Roger Bannister runs the first sub-four-minute mile.
Beethoven's Ninth Symphony is premiered in Vienna.
Coca-Cola is sold for the first time, at a pharmacy in Atlanta.
The first birth-control pill is approved in the United States.
The first transcontinental railroad is completed at Promontory Summit, Utah.
Deep Blue beats Garry Kasparov in a full chess match.
Florence Nightingale is born in Florence.
Churchill tells Parliament he has nothing to offer but blood, toil, tears and sweat.
Edward Jenner gives the first smallpox vaccination.
The first McDonald's opens in San Bernardino, California.
The first Academy Awards are presented.
The Antikythera mechanism is noticed among finds from an ancient shipwreck.
Mount St. Helens erupts.
Earth passes through the tail of Halley's Comet.
Charles Lindbergh takes off on the first solo flight across the Atlantic.
Amelia Earhart completes the first solo transatlantic flight by a woman.
Pac-Man is released in Japan.
Benjamin Franklin describes his bifocal spectacles in a letter.
Samuel Morse sends "What hath God wrought" over the first telegraph line.
Star Wars is released.
Bram Stoker's Dracula is published.
The Golden Gate Bridge opens.
Alan Turing submits "On Computable Numbers", the basis of modern computing.
Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reach the summit of Everest.
The first Indianapolis 500 is run.
The clock of Big Ben starts keeping time.

Elizabeth II is crowned in Westminster Abbey.
Ed White makes the first American spacewalk.
Henry Ford test-drives his first car, the Quadricycle.
The Apple II goes on sale.
D-Day: Allied forces land on the beaches of Normandy.
Sony introduces the Betamax video recorder.
George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four is published.
Donald Duck makes his first appearance.
The first Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race is rowed.
Jacques Cousteau is born.
Karl Drais rides the first bicycle, in Mannheim.
Pioneer 10 becomes the first spacecraft to pass the orbit of Neptune.
The Stars and Stripes is adopted as the flag of the United States.
Magna Carta is sealed at Runnymede.
Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman in space.
The Statue of Liberty arrives in New York Harbor, in crates.
Sally Ride becomes the first American woman in space.
Juneteenth: enslaved people in Texas are told they are free.
Samuel Morse is granted a patent for the telegraph.
SpaceShipOne makes the first privately funded crewed spaceflight.
Galileo is forced to recant his view that the Earth moves round the Sun.
Alan Turing is born in London.
Kenneth Arnold's sighting over Washington state gives us the phrase "flying saucer".
The rainbow flag is flown for the first time, at San Francisco Pride.
A pack of chewing gum becomes the first product scanned with a barcode.
The world's first nuclear power station begins generating, at Obninsk.
Adolphe Sax patents the saxophone.
The first iPhone goes on sale.
The Tunguska event flattens 2,000 square kilometres of Siberian forest.
Sony releases the Walkman.
Amelia Earhart disappears over the Pacific.
Karl Benz drives the first automobile in public, in Mannheim.
The Declaration of Independence is adopted.
Dolly the sheep, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, is born.
Louis Pasteur gives the first rabies vaccination.
Sliced bread is sold for the first time, in Chillicothe, Missouri.
Roswell Army Air Field announces it has recovered a "flying disc".
The first Wimbledon championship begins.
Nikola Tesla is born.
Skylab falls back to Earth over the Indian Ocean and Australia.
The Rolling Stones play their first gig, at the Marquee Club in London.
Live Aid concerts are held in London and Philadelphia.

The Rosetta Stone is found in Egypt.
Apollo 11 lifts off for the Moon.
Disneyland opens in Anaheim.
Intel is founded.
The Paris Metro opens.
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walk on the Moon.
The lowest temperature ever recorded on Earth, -89.2 C, at Vostok Station, Antarctica.
Wiley Post completes the first solo flight around the world.
William Burt patents the typographer, an early typewriter.
Hiram Bingham reaches Machu Picchu.
Louise Brown, the first baby conceived by IVF, is born.
The agency that becomes the FBI is founded.
Bugs Bunny makes his debut in "A Wild Hare".
The metric system is made legal for use in the United States.
NASA is created.
Uruguay wins the first FIFA World Cup.
The first United States patent is granted, for a way of making potash.
MTV begins broadcasting with "Video Killed the Radio Star".
The Tower Subway, the world's first tube railway, opens in London.
Columbus sets sail from Palos de la Frontera.
Dom Perignon invents champagne, by legend.
The first transatlantic telegraph cable is completed.
Tim Berners-Lee posts the first public description of the World Wide Web.
Alice Ramsey completes the first drive across the United States by a woman.
Thomas Edison patents the mimeograph.
Betty Boop makes her first appearance.
The Magellan spacecraft arrives at Venus.
Hedy Lamarr and George Antheil are granted a patent for frequency hopping.
IBM releases its Personal Computer.
Harry Brearley casts the first stainless steel, in Sheffield.
France issues the world's first driving licences.
The Woodstock festival begins.
Joseph Kittinger parachutes from a balloon 31 kilometres up.
Double Eagle II completes the first transatlantic balloon crossing.
Pierre Janssen discovers helium in the spectrum of the Sun.
The daguerreotype process is announced to the public in Paris.
Voyager 2 is launched.
The Mona Lisa is stolen from the Louvre.
The first Geneva Convention is signed.
The World Wide Web is opened to new users.
Mount Vesuvius erupts and buries Pompeii, by the traditional date.
Galileo demonstrates his telescope to the lawmakers of Venice.
Krakatoa erupts.
The first hydrogen balloon is launched, in Paris.
Martin Luther King Jr. delivers his "I Have a Dream" speech.
Michael Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction.
A comet is seen colliding with the Sun for the first time.

Google is founded.
Voyager 1 is launched.

Star Trek premieres on NBC.

Super Mario Bros. is released in Japan.

The Mayflower sets sail from Plymouth.

The New York Times publishes its first issue.

Germany is reunified.

Edison tests his first successful incandescent lamp.

Sesame Street premieres.

Mickey Mouse makes his debut in Steamboat Willie.
Lincoln delivers the Gettysburg Address.
